Wipro 3D will help manufacturers identify suitable applications and integrate composite additive manufacturing into existing production processes.
Wipro 3D, an additive manufacturing company, has entered into a strategic partnership with Markforged, a global provider of industrial 3D printing solutions, to expand access to composite 3D printing technology in India.
The partnership will combine Wipro 3D’s application engineering and manufacturing expertise with Markforged’s Continuous Fiber Reinforcement (CFR) technology to help manufacturers across aerospace, defence, automotive, energy and heavy engineering produce strong, lightweight components while reducing production lead times.
Markforged’s composite 3D printers support applications ranging from functional prototypes and customised industrial components to manufacturing tools, jigs and fixtures. The technology enables manufacturers to produce durable, lightweight parts while offering greater flexibility in design and production, the companies said in a joint communique.
Under the partnership, Wipro 3D will help manufacturers identify suitable applications and integrate composite additive manufacturing into existing production processes.
“Our customers are looking for ways to shorten development cycles and produce tooling and components suited to their manufacturing needs. Partnering with Markforged expands Wipro 3D’s industrial additive manufacturing portfolio and enables us to address a broader range of applications. By bringing together Markforged’s composite printing technology and our application engineering expertise, we aim to make advanced additive manufacturing more accessible and relevant to Indian manufacturers, helping them translate its potential into practical outcomes on the factory floor,” said Yathiraj Kasal, General Manager and Business Head, Wipro 3D.
Ashan Dhunna, Country Head and Sales Director, Markforged, said India offered significant opportunities for composite 3D printing across product development and industrial production.
“Wipro 3D’s engineering capabilities and understanding of local manufacturing requirements make it a strong partner for expanding access to our technology. Together, we look forward to helping more Indian manufacturers adopt continuous fiber reinforcement for applications that demand strength, low weight and manufacturing flexibility,” he said.
The collaboration will also focus on developing in-house composite additive manufacturing capabilities among Indian manufacturers, enabling faster product development and greater flexibility in producing application-specific components and tools.
